hypothesis: Five patterns without a proven equivalence in docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md section 6 (Observer, Bridge, Flyweight, Command, Prototype) can be modeled with the kernel's existing arrows and path equations, but each candidate weak lens buys zero unique detections over a scripted conventional test; parity or a null result is the expected deliverable.
comparison_rule: unique = probe_elements - baseline_elements; an element is the named witness listed per fault. Both arms name elements in the same vocabulary; a finding counts only when its mapped element is in the pre-registered set.

observer.lens: subject x event = seen (delivered event is the subject's current event)
observer.gap: notification totality over dynamically registered observers is not expressible: the model names the observer rows and their subject edges up front, so registration changes are outside the check

bridge.lens: impl x impl_op = op (the abstraction delegates its result to the implementor)
bridge.gap: independent variation of the abstraction and implementation hierarchies is not expressible; only one declared delegation path is checked

flyweight.lens: client -> key -> factory and client -> flyweight name one shared instance
flyweight.gap: object identity / share count has no predicate in the kernel surface; two flyweight rows with equal intrinsic values are indistinguishable from one shared row, so the duplicate fixture emits zero findings

command.lens: after x undo = before and before x redo = after (the command's inverse pair)
command.gap: command history, queue order, and receiver dispatch are temporal/behavioral and not expressible; the model pre-declares the before/after states, so a missing undo registration cannot be discovered

prototype.lens: clone x intrinsic = source x intrinsic (the clone image preserves intrinsic value)
prototype.gap: aliasing and mutation independence (deep vs shallow copy) are not expressible by static path equality; the check sees declared values, never later mutation
